problems.question: The Earth generates a magnetic field and therefore has magnetic poles. Assume that the north pole of a compass magnet points north. Where is the Earth's magnetic south pole located?
options: On the South Pole
On the North Pole
At the center of the Earth
At some point around the equator
problems.hint: Opposite magnetic poles attract each other.
problems.detailed: Since the north pole of a compass magnet is attracted toward Earth's geographic North Pole, the Earth must behave like a magnetic south pole at that location. Therefore, Earth's magnetic south pole is located near the geographic North Pole.
problems.author: Doyoon Kim

problems.question: Which of the following statements about magnetic field lines is NOT true?
options: The direction of the magnetic field is tangent to the field line at any point in space.
The strength of the field is proportional to the density of the field lines.
Magnetic field lines can never cross.
Magnetic field lines are directed from the south pole to the north pole.
problems.hint: Recall the conventional direction of magnetic field lines outside a magnet.
problems.detailed: Magnetic field lines are conventionally defined as emerging from the north pole and entering the south pole outside the magnet. Therefore, the statement claiming the opposite direction is incorrect.
problems.author: Doyoon Kim

problems.question: Some objects are attracted to magnets because they become magnetized. Which of the following materials is attracted to magnets?
options: Diamond
Gold
Cobalt
Water
problems.hint: Only one of these materials is paramagnetic.
problems.detailed: Cobalt is a paramagnetic material and is attracted to magnetic fields. Diamond, gold, and water are diamagnetic and are weakly repelled by magnetic fields.
problems.author: Doyoon Kim

problems.question: What happens to a magnet when it is heated?
options: It becomes weaker
It becomes stronger
Its strength does not change
Its poles swap places
problems.hint: Thermal motion affects magnetic domain alignment.
problems.detailed: Heating a magnet increases thermal agitation, which disrupts the alignment of magnetic domains. As a result, the magnet becomes weaker.
problems.author: Doyoon Kim

problems.question: Which description correctly represents the magnetic field inside a bar magnet?
options: Field lines start at the center and move outward
Field lines begin at the south pole and end at the north pole
Field lines form continuous closed loops
Field lines terminate at the poles
problems.hint: Magnetic field lines never begin or end.
problems.detailed: Magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops. Inside the magnet, the field lines travel from the south pole to the north pole, completing the loop.
problems.author: Doyoon Kim

problems.question: Which statement correctly describes magnetic field lines around a bar magnet?
options: They exit the south pole and enter the north pole
They exit the north pole and enter the south pole
They only exist outside the magnet
They are random in direction
problems.hint: Remember the conventional direction of magnetic field lines.
problems.detailed: By convention, magnetic field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole outside the magnet. This direction defines the orientation of the magnetic field.
problems.author: Doyoon Kim
